review_type: string parser allocation and cleanup review

scope.duplicate_representation_note: kfree at lines 139 and 315 is each represented twice by Joern with cast/type variants; each is one source call.

findings.details: Empty input returns a one-byte zeroed allocation (or NULL on allocation failure) with output length zero. Failure to allocate s_copy returns NULL and length zero. Failure to allocate out_buf frees s_copy before returning. Normal parsing frees s_copy once, sets the output length, and returns out_buf to the caller; this is ownership transfer, so the absence of an in-function kfree(out_buf) is expected. The two kfree sites are disjoint control-flow paths.

Four output-bound guards call __break and then goto LABEL_77. The C mirror defs.h maps __break to pr_warn, which returns; LABEL_77 sets the output length to zero and returns without freeing s_copy. If one of those guards fires when this C path is used, s_copy leaks (out_buf is returned to the caller, so its ownership is separate). Ghidra marks the corresponding stock branch as a non-returning SoftwareBreakpoint and the exact assembly contains BRK #1. The Makefile filters out string_change.c and links syna_string_change_exact.S, so the current candidate runtime retains the stock trap and does not take this returning C fallback. The 3*strlen allocation and per-write bounds checks make guard activation unlikely for ordinary valid input, but this pass did not prove an invariant over all malformed strings.
